observations.observed: Multiple elongated, smooth, curvilinear soft-tissue opacities are distributed throughout the mid and lower abdomen bilaterally, coiled and looping within gas-filled bowel loops. The surrounding dark bowel gas outlines these structures clearly. This is a static image with no motion artifact.

observations.expected: The visible anatomy matches the requested supine abdomen cropped at the iliac crests with the pelvis and groin completely out of frame and the declared age and anatomical exceptions.
observations.observed: The image is an AP supine abdominal radiograph extending from the lower thorax to approximately the iliac crest level; the pelvis and groin are not included. Lumbar vertebrae appear appropriate for a child with open-appearing growth plates where discernible. Bowel gas pattern is continuous and anatomically distributed. No duplicated organs, extra bones, or impossible structures are identified. No lettering or side markers are present.

findings: AP supine abdominal radiograph extending from lower thorax to pelvis

Multiple curvilinear/tubular radio-opaque structures distributed throughout the mid and lower abdomen bilaterally, consistent in morphology with helminth/parasitic worms (elongated, smooth-bordered densities)
These structures demonstrate characteristic curved and coiled configurations in the mid-abdomen and lower quadrants
Large volume of gas-filled bowel loops visible throughout the abdomen
Lumbar spine is midline; vertebral bodies appear intact without obvious lytic or sclerotic lesion
Lower ribs partially visualised; no obvious rib fracture seen
No obvious pneumoperitoneum on supine view
No calcified renal or gallbladder calculi identified
Liver and spleen soft-tissue shadows not clearly demarcated
Pelvic structures not fully included in field of view
differential: Ascariasis (Ascaris lumbricoides) — most likely; the numerous elongated curvilinear opacities are classic for heavy ascaris infestation within the intestinal lumen
Heavy mixed helminthiasis (e.g. concurrent Trichuris or other roundworm species) — cannot exclude co-infection given volume of worms
Barium-filled bowel loops — less likely as opacities are discrete worm-like structures rather than continuous lumen opacification; barium would coat mucosa differently
anatomyConcerns: The sheer number and distribution of worm-like opacities is striking and indicates very heavy parasite burden, likely causing or at risk of causing intestinal obstruction
No pneumoperitoneum or evidence of perforation identified on this supine view, but clinical correlation is essential
Pelvis is not fully included, limiting assessment of pelvic structures
Supine projection limits detection of free air; erect or decubitus view would improve sensitivity for perforation

imageApproval.diagnosticReason: Numerous elongated smooth curvilinear soft-tissue densities distributed throughout the mid and lower abdomen, outlined by surrounding luminal gas, are morphologically characteristic of Ascaris lumbricoides worms in heavy intestinal infestation. The discrete worm-like structures differ from barium coating or other luminal opacification patterns. Clinical context of crampy pain and vomiting in a child further supports this. No equally or better supported alternative diagnosis is visible.
